item.title: Databricks Raises $5 Billion at a $190 Billion Valuation
item.description: Databricks Inc. has secured $5 billion in funding at a valuation of $190 billion, the second round of financing this year for a fast-growing software firm that competes with Snowflake Inc. and Alphabet Inc.

item.title: Foreign Investors Flee Brazil Stocks at Fastest Pace Since 2021
item.description: Foreign investors pulled money out of Brazilian equities on Tuesday at the fastest pace in over five years as concerns over the presidential election make them increasingly wary of the outlook for the fiscal deficit and the economy.

item.title: Traders Pare Bets on Fed Rate Hike This Year as Oil Prices Fall
item.description: Bond traders stopped fully pricing in a Federal Reserve interest-rate increase this year amid a retreat in oil prices that reinforced positive sentiment on the inflation outlook.

item.title: Goldman’s Kaplan Backs ‘Kick-the-Can’ Fed Caution on Rate Hikes
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s Robert Kaplan said the Federal Reserve made “absolutely” the right call by not raising interest rates in July and urged policymakers to keep an open mind through September, citing a complex mix of inflationary and disinflationary “crosscurrents” making rigid forward guidance counterproductive.

item.title: The Ultimate Tax Deferral: Inside the 351 Conversion ETF
item.description: ETFs are already famous for their tax efficiency, but this popular corner of the market is pushing those benefits further than ever.

item.title: Carney Walks a Political Tightrope as US Trade Talks Approach Deadline
item.description: A year ago, after a meeting with Canada’s provincial leaders, Prime Minister Mark Carney made a pledge that he has since repeated many times.

item.title: Fed’s Hammack Questions Whether US Inflation Will Keep Slowing
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack questioned whether recent signs of a slowdown in inflation will continue and reiterated her call to raise interest rates now.

item.title: Chinese Talent Plans Brought to Light With Science Agency Probe of Professor
item.description: Tao Li failed to disclose participation in Chinese talent plans while helping to award US research money, probe concludes.

item.title: Flock Cameras Get New Privacy Guardrails as CEO Says ‘We’re Not Big Brother’
item.description: Flock Safety plans to establish new guardrails for its technology following backlash over allegations that its automated license plate readers are being misused and enabling mass surveillance.

item.title: DeepSeek Increases Prices for AI Services by Multiple Times
item.description: DeepSeek is steeply raising the prices for its flagship V4 models, bringing the low-cost provider’s rates closer to those of major artificial intelligence rivals.

item.title: Air India Orders One-Off Drug Test for Its Over 5,000 Pilots
item.description: Air India Group will screen its more than 5,000 pilots for psychoactive substances in an unprecedented one-time action, according to an internal email, after a captain allegedly tested positive for illegal drugs following the mid-air plunge of its Phuket-Delhi flight.

item.title: US Jobless Claims Edged Up to 209,000 Last Week
item.description: Filings for US unemployment benefits rose last week after hovering near historic lows.

item.title: US Producer Price Growth Decelerates by More Than Forecast
item.description: US wholesale inflation decelerated in July from a year earlier by more than estimated, helped by a further decline in energy and food costs.

item.title: Surveillance Dronemaker Tekever in Talks for Funding at €5.5 Billion Valuation
item.description: Tekever, a Portuguese developer of surveillance drones, is in talks with investors to raise as much as €500 million ($577 million) at a €5.5 billion valuation, a fivefold jump from last year.

item.title: Frasers Group Buys Harvey Nichols Out of Insolvency, Beating Next
item.description: Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group Plc acquired struggling Harvey Nichols out of insolvency, beating out rival retailer Next Plc for the storied British department store chain after it fell on hard times.

item.title: Taiwan Warns Against Uganda Travel as Passport Disputes Grow
item.description: Taiwan urged citizens to postpone travel to Uganda after a series of passport disputes, the latest sign of growing pressure on the island’s international presence in Africa.

item.title: New Institutional Investor Set to Fuel Chile Capital Market Boom
item.description: Chile has a new institutional investor poised to plow billions of dollars into corporate bonds over the next few years, just as local pension funds are raking in more money than ever, promising a boon for domestic borrowers.

item.title: US Fuel Prices Will Likely Stay High for a While
item.description: Costs at the pump are unlikely to come down significantly until Donald Trump can strike a lasting deal with Iran.

item.title: US Tech Earnings Shock Would Ripple Through UK, BOE Says
item.description: The fallout from an artificial intelligence stock bubble bursting would spread to the UK, hitting share prices, gilt yields and corporate credit markets, according to Bank of England analysis.

item.title: Meta Faces Big Tobacco Moment in Youth Harm Trial Brought by AGs
item.description: The company risks a huge monetary penalty and forced product changes

item.title: UK Economy Shrugs Off Iran War Shock for Now
item.description: Sizzling weather and World Cup fever helped output comfortably outperform expectations.

item.title: Africa’s Top Insurer Returns to Zimbabwe Market After Six Years
item.description: Shares in Old Mutual Ltd. began trading on Zimbabwe’s dollar-denominated stock exchange, six years after they were suspended on the country’s main bourse to curb a currency rout.

item.title: JLR Owner Misses Profit Estimate Stung by Luxury Unit Slack
item.description: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd., the parent of Jaguar Land Rover, reported a lower-than-expected quarterly profit, as the weakness in its UK luxury unit offset strong sales in India.

item.title: Big Tech Drives Up Credit Risk for Safe Firms With No AI Links
item.description: As a flood of debt sales by US tech companies ripples through the credit market, it seems to be triggering an inadvertent rise in risk metrics for some of the world’s safest firms.

item.title: Workers Don Motion Trackers, Cameras to Teach AI Their Jobs
item.description: They are providing robots valuable data on the very essence of human movement.

item.title: Sri Lanka Reducing Reliance on Foreign Debt, Short-Term Bills
item.description: Sri Lanka is reducing dependence on foreign borrowing while raising more money domestically through longer-term bonds, as it seeks to make its debt more sustainable under an International Monetary Fund program, Deputy Finance Minister Anil Jayantha Fernando said.

item.title: China’s Didi Returns to Profit on Strong Domestic Ride Demand
item.description: Didi Global Inc. swung back to profit after two consecutive quarterly losses, helped by strong ride-hailing demand in China.

item.title: Thai Hotel Giant Minor International Delays $1 Billion REIT Plan
item.description: Minor International Pcl, Thailand’s biggest hotel and restaurant operator, postponed plans for its first real estate investment trust, valued at about $1 billion, as market conditions soured.

item.title: JD.com Logs First Sales Fall in Latest Sign of Consumer Malaise
item.description: JD.com Inc. posted its first quarterly revenue decline since listing in 2014, in the latest sign of waning Chinese consumer sentiment.
